name: Angevins to Roses: Three Centuries of Plantagenet Kings
description: Henry II's sons, a charter wrung from a king, plague, the Hundred Years' War and the civil wars that ended with Richard III dead at Bosworth.

checkpoints.name: Henry II and his sons
checkpoints.note: Henry II's Plantagenet realm reached from the Scottish border to the Pyrenees, with his wife Eleanor of Aquitaine bringing great lands in France. Their son Richard the Lionheart led the Third Crusade, where he faced Saladin, and died in 1199.

checkpoints.name: Charter and abbey
checkpoints.note: Under King John, who lost Normandy in 1204, rebel barons forced him in 1215 to seal Magna Carta, which limited royal power under law. Later Henry III began rebuilding Westminster Abbey in the new Gothic style.

checkpoints.name: War and plague
checkpoints.note: In 1337 Edward III claimed the French crown, beginning the Hundred Years' War, in which the longbow won famous victories. The Black Death killed a large share of England's people from 1348, the Peasants' Revolt came in 1381, and Geoffrey Chaucer wrote The Canterbury Tales.

checkpoints.name: Agincourt and Joan
checkpoints.note: Henry V won at Agincourt in 1415 and came close to joining the English and French crowns. Joan of Arc then inspired French forces, was tried and executed in 1431, and by 1453 the war ended with England losing nearly all its French lands.

checkpoints.name: The Wars of the Roses
checkpoints.note: Rival branches, Lancaster and York, fought for the crown from 1455. Richard III took the throne in 1483, after his two nephews were last seen in the Tower of London. Henry Tudor beat him at Bosworth Field in 1485 and, as Henry VII, founded the House of Tudor.
